metadata.source: Curated Real NASA & CSA Dataset (PDS MEDA • DONKI • RadLab • OSDR • Mars Trek)
metadata.auditNote: Immutable curated training scenarios, not live telemetry. Official links provide provenance and review context; values must not be described as live measurements.

sols.title: MEDA Sol 15 Clear Morning — Jezero Crater
sols.donkiAlert: MEDA Sol 15 archive profile • Radio check nominal; Shield [3] remains on watch.
sols.osdrFinding: OSD-104 and OSD-379 document muscle, bone, and unloading research; exercise is a training countermeasure for reduced-gravity missions.
sols.csaFoodStatus: CSA hydroponics context supports warm recirculating trays; the 0.84 kg O₂/day figure is a crew-use gameplay reference, not a measured tray output.
recordCitations: NASA PDS Mars 2020 MEDA Sol 15 profile • https://pds-atmospheres.nmsu.edu/data_and_services/atmospheres_data/Mars2020/mars2020.html
NASA OSDR OSD-104 and OSD-379 • https://osdr.nasa.gov/bio/repo/
NASA RadLab / MSL RAD baseline and ISS comparison • https://visualization.osdr.nasa.gov/radlab/
sols.archiveNote: Curated Sol 15 training profile with a −22.4°C daily-high and −83.0°C night-low input; not live telemetry. PDS row-level provenance should be checked before calling values raw instrument readings.

sols.missionBrief: Sol 15 clear-morning training profile: daily high −22.4°C, night low −83.0°C, pressure 742.5 Pa, wind 4.2 m/s ESE, Tau 0.45, and RadLab baseline 210 µGy/day.
sols.optimalTradeoffHint: Low thermal and shielding demand. Route power to Suit Thrusters & Life Support to complete calibration quickly.

sols.title: MEDA Sol 117 Convective Dust Vortex
sols.donkiAlert: MEDA Sol 117 archive profile • 24.3 Pa pressure-drop training scenario; Shield [3] protects comms.
sols.osdrFinding: OSD-482 is linked for judge review. The enclosed-habitat filtration summary is a training interpretation, not a quotation of the study title.
sols.csaFoodStatus: CSA lettuce and radish trays need warm roots while dusty solar power is weak; boost Thermal [2] before harvesting.
sols.marsTrekCoords: 18.4447°N, 77.4508°E • Elev -2,540m • Neretva Vallis Delta Training Sector
recordCitations: NASA PDS Mars 2020 MEDA Sol 117 pressure-vortex profile • https://pds-atmospheres.nmsu.edu/data_and_services/atmospheres_data/Mars2020/mars2020.html

sols.missionBrief: MEDA barometers detect a 24.3 Pa pressure drop to 718.2 Pa. A convective vortex brings 19.8 m/s gusts, Tau 1.65, and 290 W/m² irradiance.
sols.optimalTradeoffHint: Visibility is dropping fast and wind drag is high. Boost Visor LiDAR/HUD and Suit Thrusters to reach the Solar Array and clear the panels.

sols.title: MEDA Sol 68 Deep Night Thermal Plunge
sols.donkiAlert: MEDA Sol 68 night archive profile • No SEP spike tonight; protect crop plumbing.
sols.osdrFinding: The CSA toolkit supplies hydroponic food-production context; plant biology findings should be read directly from linked OSDR studies.
sols.csaFoodStatus: Training root-zone target: +20°C to +24°C for dwarf wheat, red leaf lettuce, and radish trays. The 0.84 kg O₂/day value is a crew-use reference, not a CSA tray measurement.
sols.marsTrekCoords: 18.4447°N, 77.4508°E • Elev -2,540m • Crater Rim Ridge Night Shelter

sols.missionBrief: Sol 68 night profile: −84.6°C air, −88.2°C ground brightness temperature, 755.0 Pa, and 0.0 W/m² irradiance. Protect the greenhouse plumbing.
sols.optimalTradeoffHint: CRITICAL THERMAL WARNING: Divert at least 55% power to Thermal Heaters immediately or your suit and hydroponics will freeze.

sols.title: DONKI X-Class Solar Particle Event
sols.donkiAlert: DONKI 2024-05-14T16:46:00-FLR-001 • CME 1,250 km/s archive scenario; boost Shield [3].
sols.osdrFinding: OSD-321 and OSD-51 are linked for radiation-biology review. DNA-repair and immune-response wording is a training summary, not a direct study quotation.
sols.csaFoodStatus: CSA crops stay warm, but radiation alarms take priority; shift power to Shield [3], then harvest when the alert clears.

sols.missionBrief: RAD training spike: 4,850 µGy/day (23× the 210 µGy/day baseline). DONKI X-class flare and 1,250 km/s CME context drive the ultraviolet-aurora alert.
sols.optimalTradeoffHint: Divert maximum wattage to the Outpost Magnetic Shield Generator and hurry to the Radar Tower to lock the emergency deflector.

sols.title: PDS Regional Dust Storm Peak — Tau 3.40
sols.donkiAlert: PDS opacity Tau 3.40 archive scenario • 89% sunlight blocked; conserve power and protect the outpost.
sols.osdrFinding: OSD-104 muscle research reminds crews that 0.38g still requires exercise; save enough Mobility [1] to reach shelter safely.
sols.csaFoodStatus: CSA recirculating trays lose sunlight and warmth in the storm; alternate Thermal [2] with Mobility [1] to reach the greenhouse.
sols.marsTrekCoords: 18.4447°N, 77.4508°E • Elev -2,540m • Neretva Vallis Delta Storm Route
sols.archiveNote: Curated dust-storm training profile: Tau 3.40, 28.4 m/s wind, 695.4 Pa, −56.2°C air, and 65.0 W/m² irradiance representing 89% blockage; not live telemetry.

sols.missionBrief: Atmospheric opacity Tau 3.40 blocks 89% of sunlight, leaving 65.0 W/m². Winds reach 28.4 m/s, pressure is 695.4 Pa, and air temperature is −56.2°C.
sols.optimalTradeoffHint: Dynamically juggle power between Thermal Heaters, Visor LiDAR, and Shield/Thrusters in real time to reach the Perseverance Rover.
